description: Homelab policy: routine updates self-merge after CI. Data stores, Home Assistant runtimes, critical platform majors, and custom-image rebuilds require manual review because rollback is stateful or coordinated.

No managerFilePatterns overrides here on purpose: Renovate MERGES those with its defaults rather than replacing them, so narrowing to apps/ and pico/ would have added nothing while implying a restriction that does not exist. The defaults already cover apps/*/Chart.yaml, apps/*/values.yaml, pico/*/compose.yaml, cilium/Chart.yaml, terraform/*.tf and .github/workflows/*.

Renovate branches are validated by the infrastructure CI workflow before automerge. Helm archives are never committed: CI and ArgoCD rebuild the exact dependencies in Chart.lock, preventing a stale charts/*.tgz from shadowing a version bump.

rebaseWhen is 'conflicted', not 'behind-base-branch'. With behind-base-branch, every merge left the remaining branches behind main, so Renovate had to rebase them and could only merge them on a LATER run — the queue drained about 2 PRs per run instead of all at once. These PRs touch disjoint files (one values.yaml or compose.yaml each), so they do not actually conflict, and main has no branch protection requiring an up-to-date branch. 'conflicted' rebases only on a real conflict and lets the rest merge immediately.
Bare `image: repo:tag` lines inside chart TEMPLATES, which no built-in manager reads — currently busybox in apps/gym-booker/templates/deployment.yaml.

Scoped to templates/ only, deliberately. It used to cover apps/*/values.yaml too, but helm-values already models those (kubectl and distroless-iptables in apps/ttyd/values.yaml), so both managers found the same dep and Renovate opened two PRs for it — #23 renovate/apps-ttyd and #24 renovate/kubernetes-images.

customManagers.description: Pinned ArgoCD upstream manifest release used by bootstrap and upgrades.

packageRules.description: Huginn's existing data directory is MySQL 5.7 format. Never propose a direct current-major jump; changing this boundary requires a staged logical migration and a matching CI guard update.

description: 1. DATA LAYER — never self-merge. A bad Postgres/MySQL/MariaDB major means a restore, not a rollback. These open a PR and wait for Steve.

Regex, not globs: depNames here are a mix of bare (`mysql`, `redis`, `cloudnative-pg`) and registry-qualified (`ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres`), and a `**mysql**` glob does not reliably match a name with no path separators. Substring regex matches both forms. Checked against the real dependency set — `phpmyadmin` does not collide.
2. Self-built images. Tagged with a git SHA or built by hand on pico — Renovate has no upstream to compare against and would only churn. The GitHub Actions that build them own their versioning.

Regex again — Renovate reports these fully qualified (`docker.io/stevegore/ttyd`, not `stevegore/ttyd`), so a `stevegore/**` glob anchored at the start would miss them. The bare names are images built on pico that exist in no registry at all.

packageRules.description: 3. Floating tags are pinned to their current digest so every deployment receives an auditable Git change.
Home Assistant runtime updates require a verified backup and migration review.
Portainer controls every git-backed pico stack. Hold all of its updates for a cold portainer_data backup and post-migration API/stack verification.
Critical platform major upgrades require manual review.
ArgoCD upgrades are manual because it reconciles the rest of the platform.
4. Kubernetes-adjacent images carry ordering constraints with the OKE control plane (currently v1.36.x). Group them so kubectl/iptables/etc. move together in one PR rather than racing each other.
5. Chart + image for the same app land together, so ArgoCD does one sync instead of two.
6. GitHub Actions: batch into one weekly PR — the workflows are not load-bearing enough to warrant individual PRs.
7. The caddy Dockerfile builds a custom binary. A base-image bump needs a manual buildx push + tag bump in values.yaml (see apps/caddy/Dockerfile), so it cannot self-merge.
prBodyNotes:
:warning: Merging this is **not** enough. Rebuild and push the image, then bump `image.tag` in `apps/caddy/values.yaml`:
```
docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 \
  -t syd.ocir.io/sdajdczqv0qo/caddy:<new-tag> --push apps/caddy/
```

packageRules.description: 8. The Garmin MCP Dockerfile is a self-built image. Its base-image updates need a manual image rebuild and deployment tag bump.

description: 9. The helm binary CI validates with must track the one ArgoCD renders with (Helm 3). This is not a workflow-tooling bump like the rest of rule 6: it changes what `scripts/validate-version-upgrades.sh` actually tests.

Renovate's github-actions manager reads azure/setup-helm's `version:` input as the `helm` dep (packageName helm/helm, depType uses-with). PR #52 grouped it into 'github actions', which automerges, and it went v3.21.3 -> v4.2.3 on 2026-08-03 (commit b7bb4ca). CI validated Helm 4 against a Helm 3 renderer until 2026-08-10.

The cap is on the major only, deliberately: Helm 3.x patches still flow through the weekly actions group untouched. Lift allowedVersions and the pin in .github/workflows/validate.yml together, once ArgoCD renders with Helm 4 and the Authentik repository regression noted there is resolved.
